I contacted the office to schedule an initial consultation with Ms. Vaughn and asked if I could email a brief summary of my issue along with two one-page documents for her to review beforehand. I was told this was not permitted.

With a $150 consultation fee and a $450 hourly rate, I expected at least the opportunity to briefly explain the matter and determine whether the attorney could assist before deciding to retain her.

owner_reply:
Thank you for sharing your feedback. We take all client and prospective client experiences seriously, and we would like to clarify a few points for anyone reviewing this feedback.

First, we do not have any staff member named Patrick at our firm, and we are unable to speak to that portion of your review. That said, we sincerely apologize if you were interacted with by anyone who was not courteous and professional, that is a standard this firm always strives to achieve, and we take it seriously any time it appears we may have fallen short.

Second, as a matter of firm policy, we do not review documents submitted by email prior to a scheduled consultation. An initial consultation serves several purposes: it allows the attorney to get to know you and your matter, assess whether you have a viable case, determine whether our firm is in a position to take it on, and allow you to decide whether you would like to move forward with our firm. We have found this is best accomplished through direct conversation rather than a written submission reviewed in advance.

It is also important to note that no attorney-client relationship exists until both parties agree to enter into one, which typically occurs at the conclusion of the consultation. Documents provided beforehand may therefore not be protected by attorney-client privilege. We decline to collect documents prior to a consultation specifically to protect prospective clients from inadvertently sharing sensitive information without the benefit of that protection. We also keep our consultation fee limited to the time spent on the call itself, rather than billing for document review conducted in advance.

We are glad you found representation that met your needs, and we wish you the best with your matter. Should you wish to discuss this further, we welcome the opportunity to speak with you directly and invite you to contact our office.
